title: Per-row permission predicates in GraphQL resolvers are memoized per request on flask g
answers: mlflowSearchRuns slow with many runs because of auth queries
N+1 grants query in GraphQL authorization
how to cache permission lookups across nested GraphQL resolutions
runs table latency caused by modelVersions permission checks
body:
Symptom: listing runs in the UI (up to 100 per page) gets slower once nested model-version filtering is on, because each run triggers its own user lookup and grants query.
Root cause: a nested field is resolved once per parent row, and building a read predicate such as _rm_or_prompt_read_predicate costs a user lookup plus a SQL grants query each time.
Fix pattern: memoize the predicate for the current request in GraphQLAuthorizationMiddleware._model_version_read_predicate, storing it in the flask `g` context keyed by username (g.setdefault("_graphql_model_version_read_predicates", {})), and reuse it for every resolution in that request.
Constraints: the cache lives only for one request, so grant changes made during a request are not expected to be seen; do not share it across requests. Reuse the same cached helper for top-level and nested paths so they agree.
Applies: any resolver or filter that runs once per row in a list query inside the auth GraphQL middleware.
applies: Permission helpers invoked per row of a GraphQL list result in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py.
says: The runs table loads very slowly when filtering runs by nested model versions.
Viewing one hundred runs per page takes too long to display authorization results.
Speed up the experiments runs list when checking permissions for registered model versions.
Make the runs overview table responsive when displaying rows with model version checks.
search: To prevent N+1 authorization queries when listing runs in GraphQL, memoize per-row model-version read predicates on flask g for the duration of a single request. GraphQLAuthorizationMiddleware._model_version_read_predicate stores the predicate keyed by username in g.setdefault('_graphql_model_version_read_predicates', {}) and reuses it across resolutions in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py. The cache must not be shared across requests, grant changes made during a request are not seen, and top-level and nested paths must reuse the same helper.
